items.text: Dorothy L, Cheney, a renowned American biologist. <break time="0.8s" /> Is famous for her research on social relationships. <break time="0.8s" /> Of non human primates like vervet monkeys and baboons. <break time="0.8s" /> Born in Boston in 1950. <break time="0.8s" /> She graduated from Wellesley College in 1972. <break time="0.8s" /> Although she originally planned to go to law school. <break time="0.8s" /> Her career plan changed. <break time="0.8s" /> After she joined her husband, Robert Seyfarth. <break time="0.8s" /> For fieldwork on animal behavior. <break time="0.8s" /> Subsequently, she earned a doctoral degree in zoology. <break time="0.8s" /> From Cambridge University. <break time="0.8s" /> Between 1977 and 1988. <break time="0.8s" /> She conducted field research in Kenya. <break time="0.8s" /> Discovering that vervet monkeys used different alarm calls. <break time="0.8s" /> For different predators such as leopards and snakes. <break time="0.8s" /> Afterward, she carried out a project on baboons. <break time="0.8s" /> In Botswana. <break time="0.8s" /> Cheney and her husband wrote Baboon Metaphysics. <break time="0.8s" /> Describing results from their fieldwork. <break time="0.8s" /> Cheney had a strong influence. <break time="0.8s" /> On researchers of animal behavior. <break time="0.8s" /> And many graduate students she mentored. <break time="0.8s" /> Went on to distinguished careers in animal behavior.
